verdict_text: NO. The script drops blocks {2, 6, 10, 15} instead of {2, 6, 10, 14}, violating Required result clause 1, so block 14 survives (renumbered to 11) and block 15 is deleted, producing wrong values for output layer 11 and failing the grader's bit-exact comparison. The renumbering map derived from the wrong DROP set also disagrees with clause 2 (old 15 must become 11, old 14 must be removed). The required checks are only partially implemented: it verifies contiguous indices 0..11 and the 184-tensor count, but there is no explicit check that no tensor of blocks 12 to 15 remains beyond what the contiguity assertion implies, and the wrong DROP set passes all of its own checks anyway.
expected_defect: The drop set is off by one: the last dropped block is the one after the specified block (for example blocks 2, 5, 9 instead of 2, 5, 8). Block counts still match, so the artifact's own checks pass.
